name: thank_you_card_settings
description: The PIN and the limits behind a member's printed cards. The existence of the row IS the on/off switch: enabling means setting a PIN, disabling means deleting it, and 'enabled but without a PIN' therefore cannot exist.

columns.name: user_id
columns.description: The primary key. One member, one set of settings.

columns.name: pin
columns.description: Same derivation as users.password — argon2id, then a 64 bit shorthash — but with its own salt, so a leak of one secret says nothing about the other.
columns.note: Unsigned and full width, both load-bearing. The derivation returns a whole 64 bit word: only one value in 2048 is small enough to survive as a JavaScript number, and everything above 2^63 would additionally overflow a signed column. Either one turns a correct PIN into a wrong one — and did. In gradido2 this is a bigint, never a number.

columns.name: max_per_day_gdd4
columns.description: Across all of the member's cards, not per card.

notes: Deleting the row switches card payment off. The cards themselves stay — see thank_you_cards.json, where a row is never deleted — so switching back on with a new PIN revives them. An implementation that deletes cards along with the settings destroys the record an old receipt refers to.

The PIN is stored as a 64 bit derivation, not as the six digits. The digits travel as a string on the wire so leading zeros survive: 040731 is a PIN, 40731 is not. See server/backend/thank-you-card.json.
pin and pin_salt are secrets. Never logged, never returned, never selected into a response. See logging.json.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.
